events.description: A vehicle ahead (likely a truck) is involved in a collision or severe mechanical failure, resulting in intense flames and smoke erupting from its rear/upper section while stationary or nearly stationary on a wet highway at night. Other vehicles are present nearby but not visibly colliding during the observed interval.

Initial bright flash and rapid expansion of fire/smoke from the rear of the central vehicle in frame f2 suggests a sudden ignition event (e.g., fuel tank rupture or electrical explosion), distinct from sustained burning. This precedes the larger, more stable fire seen afterward.

A sudden, bright orange-red flash erupts from the rear of the truck ahead, accompanied by a rapidly expanding plume of smoke/fire—consistent with an explosion (e.g., tire blowout with ignition or fuel line rupture). The event is brief and intense, peaking around f1 (164.5 s) and subsiding by f2 (165.0 s).

The truck ahead appears to lose control or suffer catastrophic failure immediately after the explosion (f0–f1), evidenced by erratic motion, visible fire/smoke, and sustained abnormal illumination. The vehicle remains unstable and likely disabled through f8 (168.0 s), indicating a crash or severe incident.

A sudden, intense red-orange flash erupts from the rear of the truck in front, consistent with an explosion or catastrophic mechanical failure (e.g., tire blowout with fire/sparks). The flash is brief but significantly brighter than normal brake/tail lights and expands rapidly.

The truck ahead appears to lose control or suffer a major failure after the initial flash, evidenced by erratic light patterns, visible debris/sparks, and sustained abnormal illumination (likely fire or severe damage) through multiple frames. The vehicle remains in the lane but exhibits signs of a crash event (e.g., dragging parts, fire).

A sudden bright orange-red flash erupts above and behind the truck's cab, consistent with an explosion or catastrophic mechanical failure (e.g., fuel tank ignition). The flash is intense, brief, and expands rapidly in frames f1–f4, followed by visible smoke/fire plume.

Following the explosion, the truck appears to lose control: its rear lights remain illuminated but the vehicle drifts rightward, and by f5–f7, it is clearly off the travel lane, possibly having collided with roadside infrastructure or another vehicle (partially visible on right at f15). The sustained fire/smoke and abnormal position indicate a crash event.
